rationale.usefulness: The connected Python/PyTorch sequence, public companion code and concrete verifier-to-reward progression are highly actionable for technically prepared educators and builders. The report supplies realistic experiment and interface ideas and distinguishes CPU entry work from later GPU demands. No-code beginners and production teams need additional preparation.
rationale.impact: A substantial accessible curriculum can meaningfully improve understanding and evaluation of reasoning systems within developer education. Its potential is educational diffusion of established methods; neither a new frontier method nor measured learning effectiveness is demonstrated.
rationale.novelty: The contribution is the structured teaching sequence and video presentation, not new sampling, verification, GRPO or distillation methods. The companion book/code predate this announcement, and the report correctly avoids treating the new course as a new training breakthrough.
rationale.maturity: Eight structured videos, an existing companion repository, chapter-level code, setup/troubleshooting material and hardware guidance provide a developed educational artifact. This warrants more readiness than a newly described prototype, while unexecuted notebooks, unwatched portions of the series and unmeasured end-to-end costs preclude a near-perfect score.
rationale.openness: Apache-2.0 companion code and public course/repository guidance enable inspection and adaptation, with reproducible components and hardware alternatives. The code license does not cover the videos, book, models, datasets or teacher outputs as a whole, and exact experiment environments were not independently reproduced.

concerns: No blocking discrepancy found. The October course announcement is separated from the older companion book and repository.
Small-model math results and a working verifier do not establish general reasoning or tutoring effectiveness; the report explicitly preserves this distinction and the separate asset licenses.
